title: BIWIN Black Opal NV3500 1TB PCIe 3.0 SSD $159, BIWIN M350 500GB NVMe PCIe 4.0 $89 + Delivery ($0 C&C) @ Centre Com
body:
Deal: BIWIN Black Opal NV3500 1TB PCIe 3.0 SSD $159, BIWIN M350 500GB NVMe PCIe 4.0 $89 + Delivery ($0 C&C) @ Centre Com

[Edyolo] Check your email for $10 off Centrecom if you are subscribed. Min spend $100, and I just tried it did stack, bringing the total to $149.
[cimark] Thanks for the tip! I just checked my email and used a $10 off code from 2025 and it worked!!! Lol.
[DisasterArea] Anything dipping under $200/TB is reasonable at the moment, especialy for a mini pc or laptop where typically lower power trumps high performance.
I've got my eye on the $479 OSCOO 2TB presently (Gen5) https://amzn.asia/d/00PMiXym Further $10 off with mastercard
[denserham] That 2242 is a nice price wish it was 2230
[AustriaBargain] PCIe 3 is fine, it's higher capacity I really need though.
[GordonD] A whole lot of relatively cheap Chinese-brand gen 3 and SATA 3 SSDs have started appearing on the market.
The Chinese would have had to sell them really cheap if a market niche hadn't been created by the AI factories only wanting the very fastest with a big name backing its quality, and being willing and able to pay for that.
[Haunt] Are these recently manufactured ones, or just very old stock stores/manufacturers are trying to clear out? If it's the former, i'm happy with that development. Any supply is good at this point no matter what the gen, same goes for RAM. Even DDR4 is good for consumers.
[gakko] Oh good I just bought a $130 500gig patriot M2 today. Makes sense that ozb would punish me right away
[vos0003] At least you were loyal to your country 🫡
[imtheonewhoknocks] Oof, I feel for you mate. I had a Patriot drive die on me within 8 months of use.
Don't throw anything important on there you can't afford to lose, that's all I can say.
[chaosteve] dang that 5 year warranty looks appealing too bad no 2 or 3TB size :(
[chaosteve] true true but i rather just stick with 1 for the usb reader :( thanks for the suggest
[enjoylosing] Biwin 2tb black opal at mwave for 399 currently, its a faster model gen 4 also
[enjoylosing] https://www.mwave.com.au/products/biwin-black-opal-nv7400-2t…
[enjoylosing] Also what is usb reader setup, what does that do and how is related to SSD i want to learn about this
[scottb721] Damn, would have preferred this rather than the Pixel 2 watch lol
[Bargainian] How's the warranty handled? Do you have to send it to China or processed locally?
[enjoylosing] Everything is made in china anyway. Isn't retailer responsible for warranty not manufacturer
[DisasterArea] Under Australian law the retailer must deal with warranties and cannot force you to deal with a manufacturer directly, so buy from somwehere that treats you well.
I've taken pretty much to getting these things from Amazon as they seem quick to simply refund - although that can be a bad thing in these times of inflating prices when you want a replacement not a refund.
[enjoylosing] Do we have the choice of replacement or refund, but that might be work to argue
[Clockwerk] Worth taking a risk? Thinking of getting this for an M90Q
[cloudie9] I bought the 500gb back in Feb deal, it is an ok drive for secondary but when I tried to run it primary, it causes error during halfway windows installation. Unsure what wrong with it.
[Ciallo] Apparently it's dramless micron or YMTC TLC with maxio controller, not bad for the price, especially now even apple is using QLC chips :(
[AMLagonda] I cant get free shipping for Perth :/ and I dont have a discount code either.
